source_snapshot.items: Test connections among FPGA1, FPGA1 EROT, HMC I2C-4, HMC FRU and BMC I2C-3
source_snapshot.procedure: From BMC, run `i2cdetect -y -q 2` and combined transaction `i2ctransfer -y 2 w2@0x11 0x04 0x00 r3`; consult PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic artifact/photo and unexpected-log checks; no identity for0x11, meaning for register0x0400 or expected three-byte reply.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; substitutes physical probing/soldering for an explicit remote functional transaction.

source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the BMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2cdetect -y -q 2 i2ctransfer -y 2 w2@0x11 0x04 0x00 r3
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

test_case.test_name: Test connections between FPGA 1, FPGA 1 EROT, HMC I2C-4, HMC FRU and BMC I2C-3 — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify BMC-side functional reachability across the named BMC I2C-3, FPGA1, FPGA1 EROT, HMC I2C-4 and HMC FRU path using the defined0x11 register transaction and component-specific response evidence.
required_package: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-3 to Linux bus2 through FPGA1/EROT to HMC I2C-4 and HMC FRU
Identity of bus2 address0x11 and proof it is the intended gateway/device
Vendor register definition for write bytes0x04 0x00 and three returned bytes, including expected values/masks
Explanation of which reply fields prove each named component/hop and any separate FRU content read needed
Bus owner/driver, safe combined-transaction and scan policy, timeout/NACK criteria
BMC/HMC recovery plus relevant FPGA/EROT/FRU status/error interfaces
test_case.test_command: Map logical BMC I2C-3 to Linux bus2 and identify address0x11/register0x0400 owner; define how its three-byte response represents FPGA1/EROT/HMC/FRU reachability; collect bus ownership/error baseline; avoid broad scanning; run one approved combined write-pointer/read; decode all fields against PID/vendor spec; correlate component logs/status and confirm no new bus errors.

safety_gate: Do not run `i2cdetect -q` broadly without per-address safety approval
Confirm0x0400 is a non-mutating address-pointer/read operation for the exact0x11 device
Coordinate with driver/daemon ownership of bus2 and avoid forced or concurrent access
Execute one bounded transaction; stop on unexpected length/value, NACK, timeout, arbitration loss, stuck bus or management degradation
Do not infer all-hop health from ACK alone; preserve logs and verify components after the read
expected_evidence: PID topology showing every named component/hop and BMC I2C-3-to-bus2 mapping
BMC, FPGA1, EROT, HMC and FRU identities plus bus owner/driver baseline
Vendor excerpt for0x11 register0x0400 and three-byte field decoder
Timestamped exact transaction, stdout/stderr, exit code, latency and expected-versus-observed field matrix
Component-specific status/error/log correlation demonstrating required hop coverage
Post-read bus/component/management health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy requires BMC controller, bus, target address, vendor protocol, expected response and OOB recovery. The command may run only after BMC I2C-3-to-bus2 and0x11 ownership are proven.
